summary:
Flame in Freefall is a software-based project that explores how fire behaves in microgravity using NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets.

Our project studies research from experiments such as FLEX, FLEX-2 and SAFFIRE to understand how flames behave differently in space compared to Earth.

Using data analysis, AI/ML and interactive scenario analysis, we aim to identify flame behaviour patterns, compare combustion conditions and provide insights that can support spacecraft fire safety.

*Our Goal:* To make microgravity combustion research easier to understand and contribute to safer future space missions.
details:
Our project, Flame in Freefall, is a software-based platform that explores how flames behave in microgravity. It uses NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets and research from FLEX, FLEX-2 and SAFFIRE experiments.

The platform uses data analysis, AI/ML and interactive scenario analysis to study flame behaviour and compare different combustion conditions.

Benefits and Impact: It helps make microgravity combustion research easier to understand and supports research towards improving fire safety in spacecraft.

Tools Used: NASA PSI datasets, AI/ML, data analysis and software-based visualisation.

Creativity: Our project combines NASA's real scientific research with interactive analysis and AI-based insights.

Factors Considered: Flame behaviour, microgravity conditions, combustion patterns and astronaut safety.
